inputs.name: Finite formal power-series rings over a Noetherian ring are Noetherian
inputs.statement_used: If O is Noetherian and Sigma is finite, O[[x_s:s in Sigma]] is Noetherian.
inputs.matching: The original O is already Noetherian and every chosen variable set is finite; no domain, characteristic-zero or DVR assumption is needed.

inputs.name: Nakayama's lemma for finite modules over a local ring
inputs.statement_used: A finite module M over a local ring A is generated by lifts of a generating set of M/m_A M; equivalently M=N+m_A M implies M=N.
inputs.matching: Every module to which it is applied is finite over its displayed Noetherian local ring. Surjectivity of complete-local algebra maps is then proved by actual successive approximation, not inferred from a false finite-module hypothesis on the target algebra.

elementary_background: Finite-dimensional linear algebra over k and finite-vector-space cardinality.
Compactness and Hausdorffness of a countable inverse limit of finite discrete rings, equivalently diagonal extraction in its adic metric.
Evaluation of finitely many formal variables in a maximal ideal by completeness, and the algebraic universal property of a quotient.
A finite-dimensional module killed by the maximal ideal is a finite k-space; its square-zero extension is finite as a module over its base.
proved_here_instead_of_retained: Finiteness of all dual-number lifts from the exact PhiCond.
Actual continuous matrix-lift representability at all finite Artin levels and at their complete inverse limit.
Actual framed representability, including the same original local conditions and B-map.
Formal-torus character independence over arbitrary characteristic and zero-divisor coefficient rings.
Homogeneous kernel and relation generation, actual weight-part transport, and finite-kernel continuous sections.
The needed graded local lift for an arbitrary original local topology via an explicit square-zero interpolation ring.
Exact unquotiented framed tangent identification, obstruction classes, matrix correction, and relation independence.
not_required: A finite-generation assumption on the profinite group
A topological-group structure on each original local frame group
A domain or discrete-valuation hypothesis on O
Automorphy, rigidity, a trace-counting theorem, or an arithmetic Model
